questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: The points $A(5,3), B(-2,0)$ and $C(1,1)$ are on a circle. Find the distance between the center of the circle and center of gravity of the triangle $A B C$.

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: Find the nature of the equation $9 x^{2}-16 y^{2}+72 x-32 y-16=0$. Also find the coordinates of its centre and foci, equation of the directrices, and the length of the latus rectum.

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{1}{x}(\sqrt{1+x}-\sqrt{1-x})=?$

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: A group of 4 engineers is to be formed from 5 mechanical engineers and 4 electrical engineers working in a power plant. In how many ways can this be done so that the group contains at least one mechanical and one electrical engineer?

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: Out of two identical boxes, the first one contains 5 blue and 4 black balls; the second one contains 4 blue and 8 black balls. One box is selected at random and then one ball is drawn at random from that box. Find the probability that the ball thus drawn is blue. If the ball is blue, then what is the probability that the ball was drawn from the first box?

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: Two objects of $400 \mathrm{~g}$ and $600 \mathrm{~g}$ mass are suspended from the two ends of a rope passing over a smooth pulley. One second after starting, the heavier object is touched to stop and then released at the same time. When, after touching, the rope will again become straight?

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: A body of mass $8 \mathrm{~kg}$ falling from 10 metres of height and goes $50 \mathrm{~cm}$ inside sand and then stops. Determine the average thrust of sand on the object.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The power of the engine of a car of mass $1200 \mathrm{~kg}$ is 134.05 H.P. and the efficiency is $90 \%$. Determine the minimum time required to bring the car to a velocity of $30 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ from rest. $(1 \mathrm{H} . \mathrm{P} .=0.746 \mathrm{~kW})$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: $6000 \mathrm{MJ}$ of kinetic energy is transferred to an artificial satellite of $200 \mathrm{~kg}$ mass while it is taken to a particular altitude from the earth's surface. At what altitude will the satellite revolve around the earth? The mass of earth is $6 \times 10^{24} \mathrm{~kg}$, radius is $6400 \mathrm{~km}$ and $\mathrm{G}=6.6 \times 10^{-11} \mathrm{Nm}^{2} \mathrm{~kg}^{-2}$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A hydroelectric power plant has a dam with a height of 15 m. To generate 5 MW of power, how many kilograms of water need to fall on the turbine blades per second?

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A certain parallel plate capacitor consists of two plates, each with area $200 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$, separated by $0.4 \mathrm{~cm}$ air gap. (i) Compute the capacitance, (ii) If the capacitor is connected across $500 \mathrm{~V}$ source what energy is stored in it?

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Green light $(\lambda=555 \mathrm{~nm})$ is emitted from a $40 \mathrm{~W}$ bulb. If $3 \%$ of electrical energy is converted into light energy, how many photons are emitted from the bulb per second?

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a standard mass of $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ is placed on a moving platform, the vibration rate is $125 \mathrm{vibmin}^{-1}$. What is the mass of an unknown object for which the vibration rate is 243 vibmin $^{-1}$ ? Neglect the mass of the moving platform.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A slide projector is to project a $35 \mathrm{~mm} \times 23 \mathrm{~mm}$ slide on a $2 \mathrm{~m} \times 2 \mathrm{~m}$ screen. Determine the focal length of the lens if the screen is $10 \mathrm{~m}$ away from the lens.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A long conductor produced a single circular loop of radius, $r=0.15 \mathrm{~m}$ and other parts of this conductor remained straight. Another long conductor is placed parallel at a distance, $\mathrm{d}=0.25 \mathrm{~m}$ from the center of the loop and conducts equal current in opposite direction as shown in the figure. To produce a magnetic field of $4.72 \mu \mathrm{T}$ at the center of the loop, how much current is to be passed in each conductor? $\left[\mu_{0}=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{TmA}^{-1}\right]$[IMG: https://assets.chorcha.net/AIUXasZnQKDhQLRDwjqh4.png]

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: It has been decided to put an iron rim on a wooden wheel. The diameter of the wheel is $1.10 \mathrm{~m}$ and the inside diameter of the rim is $1.098 \mathrm{~m}$. If the rim is initially at $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, to what temperature must it be heated to just fit onto the wheel? (For iron, $\alpha=1.2 \times 10^{-5}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$ ).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text:
A piece of white phosphorous (atomic wt. $=31$ ) was thrown out in the air and caught fire. Based on this incident, answer the following questions.
(a) Write the chemical reaction that occurred in the air with physical states of the reactants and products.
(b) The amount of the product was $2.84 \mathrm{~g}$. What was the amount (in gramm) of phosphorous thrown out in the air? How many moles of phosphorous were thrown out?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: To produce $\mathrm{ZnCl}_{2}$ from $25 \mathrm{~g}$ of zinc powder, find the minimum amount (in $\mathrm{cm}^{3}$ ) of $0.05 \mathrm{moldm}^{-3} \mathrm{HCl}$ that is to be required.Question
